MESSAGE FROM THE VICE CHANCELLOR
Forensic Science occupies a distinctive position at the intersection of scientific inquiry, justice and societal responsibility. Through the systematic examination and interpretation of evidence, the discipline plays an
important role in supporting the pursuit of truth and strengthening the processes of justice. As crime and technology continue to evolve, the field calls for professionals who possess not only scientific competence but also critical thinking, ethical awareness and a commitment to continuous learning. At Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University), Bengaluru we are committed to nurturing such qualities through an education that combines academic knowledge with practical exposure and meaningful learning
experiences. The Department of Forensic Science continues to foster a dynamic learning environment by providing students with opportunities for laboratory-based learning, research, academic engagement, and exposure to emerging developments in the field, supported by state-of-the-art laboratories and advanced
research centres. It is therefore encouraging to see these efforts reflected through Veritas, the biannual newsletter of the Department of Forensic Science. Volume 6, Issue 1 brings together the academic interests, experiences, achievements and creative contributions of the Department, providing a platform for students and faculty to share their perspectives and celebrate their collective accomplishments.
I commend the editorial team, faculty members and students for their dedication in bringing this edition to fruition. Publications such as Veritas contribute to a culture of academic engagement and encourage students to communicate their ideas, explore new areas of knowledge and appreciate the wider dimensions of their
discipline. I extend my sincere wishes to the Department of Forensic Science and the editorial team for the successful publication of Volume 6, Issue 1 of Veritas. May this edition reflect the Department’s continued commitment to academic excellence, scholarly engagement and the pursuit of knowledge, while celebrating the collective efforts of its students and faculty members.
Fr. Dr. Augustine George Vice Chancellor

MESSAGE FROM DEAN
It is a pleasure to present Volume 6, Issue 1 of Veritas, the newsletter of the Department of Forensic Science, School of Biological and Forensic Sciences,Kristu Jayanti (Deemed to be University). The current edition
captures our department’s ongoing academic voyage, bringing together the insights, accomplishments, and creative expressions of both our students and faculty.Forensic science demands rigorous analytical reasoning, scientific precision, and unwavering professional integrity. To prepare our students for this evolving landscape, the Department is committed to providing an environment that extends beyond traditional classroom learning. Through hands-on laboratory experiences, immersive research, co-curricular initiatives,
and community outreach, our students learn to apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios building the confidence and ethical grounding required of forensic professionals. This volume of Veritas offers a comprehensive look into the vibrant life of our department. Inside, you will
find highlights of recent academic programs and events, alongside diverse contributions from our undergraduate and postgraduate students including in-depth case studies, book reviews, creative pieces, and updates on current trends in forensic science. I extend my heartfelt gratitude to the editorial team for their creativity, diligence, and dedication in assembling this issue. My sincere thanks also go to the faculty members, student contributors, and staff whose
efforts make Veritasan inspiring reflection of our academic community. May this issue of Veritas serve not only as a record of our recent endeavors, but as a catalyst for continued curiosity, impactful research, and professional excellence.
Warm regards and best wishes, Dr. S.Vijayanand Dean, School of Biological and Forensic Sciences

This leads to two problems: first, detecting the substance may require a more exploratory or non-targeted approach rather than a simple confirmatory test; and second, even once detected, interpreting what a concentration means in terms of impairment and time of use is done on limited grounds.

INTRODUCTION
Every crime has a story to tell, but it takes a skilled forensic expert to figure out the
truth hidden behind the evidence. Forensic explores this idea through a complicated investigation where science becomes the key to solving a series of gruesome murders.
Forensic combines the efforts of both science and law-enforcing agencies in investigating and finding the perpetrator behind the murders that take place
subsequently in the movie. This review highlights the role of forensic science in cases, the movie’s effectiveness as a crime thriller, and the accuracy of the investigative
methods portrayed.
PLOT SUMMARY
The movie starts with the abduction and murder of a young girl named Divya. This
case is assigned to ACP Rithika Xavier, who subsequently works with medico-legal advisor Samuel
John Kattookaran, known as Sam, and a forensic intern, Shikha. As the investigation progresses, more cases involving the abduction and murder of young girls are reported,
with the murders having similarities in their modus operandi. These similarities allow the investigators to suspect that the crimes are connected, prompting them to analyse
the available evidence and figure out the common link between the victims and their perpetrator.

83 FORENSIC SCIENCE ANALYSIS
One of the core aspects of Forensic is the central focus on forensic science in solving
murder. The film portrays forensics as a systematic process where evidence from the crime scene is examined to establish links between the crime, the victim, and the
possible perpetrator. The introduction of Sam shows how forensic expertise can complement traditional police investigation.
The investigations into Divya’s murder begin with statements being taken from people who were closely related to her. The crime scene is also properly
documented. The area around the fence from where Divya was abducted is photographed, helping investigators record the scene and preserve important
details. The movie also depicts good crime scene management practices.
Crime scenes are barricaded to prevent unnecessary entry, and a common pathway is created for entering and leaving the scene so that unnecessary contamination of evidence is prevented.
Evidence is also properly handled and tagged, showing the importance of
maintaining the identity and authenticity of evidence throughout an investigation. These aspects give a realistic representation of basic crime scene procedures.
Several pieces of physical and trace evidence were examined during the investigation. A bloodstained piece of cloth worn by Divya is collected for analysis.
After the analysis, three foreign samples were collected from her clothing, which included a swab containing green algae, powdered white asbestos, and droplets of
sewage water. A cross-shaped pattern is also noticed on the dress. These findings are important, as they provide clues about the environment in which a crime may have
taken place, which was also portrayed in the movie. Another interesting aspect of this movie was the portrayal of a forensic vacuum
pump to collect skin cells from a surface for DNA analysis. Since skin cells can
contain DNA, recovering them from a surface may help investigators obtain a biological profile and establish a possible connection to an individual. The film uses this technique to show how even small or
invisible traces can become useful forms of evidence.

84 STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES
One of the major strengths of Forensic is its emphasis on scientific investigation.
Unlike many crime thrillers that focus only on police work, this film highlights the role of forensic science in solving crimes.
Another strength of the film is Sam. His attention to detail, analytical thinking, and passion for forensic science make him an important part of the investigation.
Finally, the suspenseful storyline and unexpected twists keep the audience engaged throughout the film.
As for the weaknesses, the movie contains several unrealistic and overly dramatic elements. The introduction of Sam is a little dramatised and there are action
sequences involving physical confrontations between him and the killer, which is
not representative of the actual role of a medico-legal advisor. These scenes appear to have been included mainly for entertainment. Another weakness is the portrayal of forensic laboratories. While crime scenes are
shown being handled carefully, the laboratory environments did not always appear
to follow the strict contamination-control measures in this movie. In addition, some forensic results were obtained much more quickly than would
normally be possible in actual investigations. Although these changes help maintain the pace of the movie, they reduce the realism of its forensic portrayal.
OVERALL EVALUATION
Overall, Forensic introduces several important aspects of forensic investigation,
including witness examination, crime scene documentation, evidence collection and tagging, DNA examination, and medico-legal investigation.
At the same time, it exaggerates certain aspects of forensic practice for the cinematic effect. The film therefore provides an engaging portrayal of forensic
science, but its procedures should be viewed as a dramatised representation rather than an accurate depiction of real-
world forensic practice. I would rate this movie a 7.5 out of 10 and recommend it to anyone interested in
forensic science to watch this movie at least once in their lives.

Forensic science has been cast in the role of the oracle to the jury and the

systematic black-box testing-where examiners lacking the ground truth are
given samples with known provenance-for an acceptable measurement of true error rates for the so called "pattern matching" disciplines including firearms,
fingerprints and bitemarks.
2. REAL ERROR RATES BY FIELD:
A 2019 survey of forensic analysts aggregated an analysis of existing error rate
data from different disciplines. The data differed significantly from one field to the next.
Fingerprints (latent)- Error rate as low as .1% in large studies.
Bitemarks- up to a 64% false positive rate. This put bite marks on par with any of the higher error-rate disciplines, which made them a very risky

Firearms and toolmarks- this seems like an acceptable false positive rate- someplace around 1% to 2% for black-box test results depending upon how

87 3. AS THE ‘MATCH’ BECOMES MORE DIFFICULT.
In other words, error rates are not uniform. Their rates also vary dramatically
with the difficulty of the sample of matched items. A study from 2021 showed
very closely related non-matches - two distinct individuals’ fingerprints or DNA that look quite similar- have a false-positive rate ranging from 15.9 per cent to
28.1 per cent for the 11 pairs. Obviously, an average figure for an error rate is less meaningful when the stakes go up in more problematic comparisons.
4. DNA LABORATORIES
A Quality-Control Perspective. A 2014 analysis of DNA casework at the
Netherlands Forensic Institute in 2008-2012 monitored internal quality failures rather than high-profile match statistics. The rate of failures found at the NFI was
similar to those recorded in clinical and genetic-testing laboratories, indicating that even one of the most statistically rigorous forensic practices relies on
standard lab quality control standards to avoid errors.
5. PERCEPTION VERSUS REALITY
Surveys indicate jurors and general audiences systematically overestimate the
accuracy of most forensic practices, trusting DNA even above well-verified disciplines like drug and alcohol testing, despite a lack of reliable error-rate
estimates for many pattern comparison methods. As many people also conflate false positives (reporting an innocent match) with false discovery rate (likely a
claimed match is wrong), this inaccuracy could play a crucial role in courtroom results.
CONCLUSION
The statistical profile developing within the research world for the forensic
disciplines seems one of extreme variation. Many procedures are statistically sound, especially DNA, though more speculative disciplines like bitemark analysis
produce an error rate too high for use in court. As black-box studies and proficiency tests are conducted on a broader range of practices, the use of these
statistics should play a larger role in how forensic evidence is used in our system.
